notes.title: Demo Patch 0.5.4
notes.content:
Heyo!  



This demo update contains mostly small bugfixes, but also a first attempt at proper ultrawide resolution support. 

If you're using an ultrawide monitor to play Dobbel Dungeon and you still encounter issues with UI elements being misaligned after this update, please let us know!



Changelist

Implemented ultrawide resolution support

Fixed an issue where sometimes chasms (e.g. rivers) weren't properly marked as such under the hood

Fixed an issue with duplicate animation triggers.

Fixed an issue where self-targeted actions were still considered for 'apply to enemy' bonus objectives

Fixed an issue where 'Charge'-type actions would not properly end if the unit that used it died mid-action

Fixed a critical issue that could happen when you quit the tutorial mission after having dismissed the first action tutorial



Happy Dobbeling!
- Jim & Michelle

notes.title: Demo Patch 0.5.2
notes.content:
Heyo!

After watching some folks play Dobbel Dungeon live at Animecon (NL), we noticed we still had quite a few issues in the ‘clarity’ department, particularly for the more inexperienced players. 

With this update, we hope to address some of the more ‘major’ issues we noticed to hopefully get newcomers on their way faster, as well as offer some quality-of-life benefits to existing players.

Changelist

 Fixed a critical animation state issue that could happen when ‘Skip dice animations’ was enabled and you tried to dash right after manipulating a die
 Fixed missing boss battle music
 Fixed an issue where remaining overworld nodes became unavailable as soon as the boss node was revealed.
 Implemented an ‘undo movement’ button
 Improved ‘first-turn’ tutorial
 Implemented ‘resistances’ category in unit description card
 Improved unit description card layout
 Implemented (optional) end-of-turn verification
 Valid dice slots are now also highlighted when hovering over a die, instead of only when a die was being dragged

Oh, one minor side effect of this tutorial upgrade is that existing players might get a repeat of tutorial popups they've already seen. Sorry, but it's for the greater good :P

Happy Dobbeling!
- Jim & Michelle

notes.title: 🎲 Demo 0.5 is now live! 🎲
notes.content:
Heyo,

This update is a big one, where we're addressing some of the biggest points of feedback we've consistently been receiving since the demo first launched.

Big change nr. 1 is that we've added 4 difficulty modes, which should help keep the game accessible for beginners whilst keeping things interesting for more advanced players.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44829532/d89a54a054b1639d198536c91644491b008d88e4.png

Big change nr. 2 is that we've significantly changed the way the game responds to defeated heroes. Previously, when a hero was defeated, they would just be gone forever, which caused a bunch of balancing issues, confusion and generally didn't quite fit with our design goals. 

So, instead of the old permadeath system, we've changed it up so that (in most difficulties) defeated heroes will turn into ghosts. Hero ghosts will still be able to fight, but they will have ghost-specific, generally less powerful skills & stats, rather than the hero's usual stuff.

As part of the ghost system we're also introducing a new NPC: The Mystic. The mystic deals in the occult, allowing you to trade skill points for gold & vice versa, as well as allowing you to restore your ghosts back to life.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44829532/32d6fb150e7c7888400b252e25bc33e5a90542ec.png

And in case you lack the funds to restore your ghosts back to life, or just got tired of one of your heroes, the game now also allows you to swap your current party members with heroes you've previously rescued.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44829532/6833980423e1f81b8131ad4cf0673c6f1aea40ed.png

Besides those big changes. this update also contains some smaller ones, as seen in the full list below:

Changelist

 Implemented difficulty modes (4 total)
 Implemented hero ghost system
 Implemented Mystic (Quest + Shop)
 Implemented in-run hero recruitment
 Rebalanced enemies, in line with new difficulty modes
 Rebalanced hero skills and progression
 Bonus objectives now scale with run progress & difficulty mode
 Implemented controller inspection mode
 Improved enemy AI (Better performance, faster decision making & more situational awareness)
 Implemented 'auto speed up enemy turn' gameplay setting
 Implemented 'skip dice animations' gameplay setting
 Implemented (experimental) keyboard hotkeys for action management (Categories: Z-M, Actions: F1-F8, Dice: Alphanumerical 1-0)
 Implemented a 'critical health' UI overlay
 Fixed issue where enemies could spawn in inaccessible positions
 Fixed a glitch where action category buttons visually messed up their ‘selected’ state after executing an action
 Improved clay texture mapping on characters
 Fixed dialogue appearing in front of pause menu during cinematics
 Added cloud shadows
 Fixed an issue with ambush quests where heroes could occasionally spawn inside obstacles
 Fixed some inaccessible bridge issues
 When the boss node is discovered, all other uncompleted nodes now become inaccessible


We'll continue to improve these systems as development continues, so make sure to keep reporting any issues you might encounter.

Happy dobbeling!
- Jimbo

notes.title: 🎲 Demo 0.4.0 is now live! 🎲
notes.content:
Heyo,

After processing the feedback we received during December's playtest and celebrating the holidays, level generation is finally here!

In previous versions, levels were picked from a (very) limited selection of static, hand-made levels where content like (player / enemy) spawn points, obstacles and mission-critical units would always appear in the same configuration. 

Now, with this new system, that content will instead be procedurally populated based on layout templates. These layout templates are still hand-made for the time being, but they only serve to define an empty battlefield and environment. All of the content within that battlefield will be procedurally placed based on mission parameters.

We also made a couple of changes to our enemy systems to fix some jank and minimize 'unfair' situations:

Enemy spawners now operate on a token-basis, where enemies require more tokens to spawn the more powerful they are.
Enemy spawn points are now chosen based on a new rating system, rather than being (mostly) random.
Enemies will now take a penalty to initiative if they spawn within attack range of any hero.
Reworked enemy brains to be more robust in 'less than ideal' situations (mainly fixing the issue where they would sometimes just stand still and do nothing).
Most enemies can now use the Dash action.

We'll continue to rebalance and improve these systems as development continues, so make sure to keep reporting any issues you might still encounter.

Oh, and some more 'minor' stuff:

Cauterize is no longer considered an attack (which could cause things like 'flame blade' to add damage to the action's output)
Added a specific tutorial popup to explain that any damage dealt to a cage will be transfered to the prisoner inside.
Fixed some missing LODs


Happy new year!
- Jimbo

notes.title: Playtest 4.0.0 is now live!
notes.content:
Heyo,

As some of you might have noticed after playing each mission type more than once in the demo, level layouts are currently still picked from a premade pool of hand-crafted levels and are only procedurally populated with enemies inside them. 

Whilst this system was fine for the initial demo and the occasional 'special' level, I always intended for the majority of level layouts to be procedurally generated as well. Now, I'm happy to say that a first-draft version of a procedural level generation system is now functional!

I've also made some drastic changes to the way enemies are spawned across various mission types, in an attempt to address a common point of feedback regarding how current enemy spawning systems could occasionally create a situation where your party gets absolutely wrecked before you even get a chance to react.

After a bunch of internal testing and iterating, these systems have reached a point where I'm happy to share them with you. But before I merge these systems into the main demo, I'd first like to get some second opinions on their overall quality, just in case we somehow overlooked anything critical. I expect this playtest to be live for about a week, maybe a bit longer depending on how many issues are uncovered (fingers crossed).

So yeah, if you'd like to help us fine-tune these new systems, make sure to join the playtest, play a bunch of missions and fill out the survey when you're done (this survey is also accessible from the main menu)!

Happy Dobbeling!
- Jimbo

notes.title: Playtest 3 has come to an end!
notes.content:
We have closed registration for our playtest as we prepare for our upcoming demo launch!

I'd like to thank everyone who used the in-game feedback tool to tell us how they felt about the demo so far. It's very motivating to hear how much you've been able to enjoy what we've made so far and to read about the things you'd like to see us make next! 

Thanks to your help, we've also been able to fix a couple of critical bugs that managed to slip past our own eyes, as well as some smaller quality of life improvements here and there.

Your feedback matters a lot to us, so we'll make sure to keep the in-game feedback option around in the demo as long as we're still developing the main game.

Don't worry if you weren't able to join this playtest, for our demo will go live in just a couple of days. 
We'll also continue to have regular playtests as we develop more content, so keep an eye out for those too!

Thanks again, and until next time!
- Jimbo

 Loot

 Passives

If you have the time, we'd appreciate it if you could join the playtest and let us know which areas of the demo could use the most elbow grease!

notes.title: 🎲 Playtest 2 is now live! 🎲
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44829532/84ab87f91ce5a44fa234bfcb40402fe72003f680.png
Heyo!

I'm happy to share we've just updated our playtest with a new build, which primarily focuses on quest variety by adding more quest types and bonus objectives!

During the last playtest, we experimented with adding elevation to some levels to see how that could impact Dobbel Dungeon's gameplay. In our opinion, while it added some visual flair, we found it didn't really add enough value to the gameplay itself to justify the additional system complexity and related issues that came with it, especially since we're only a 2-person team. So for this playtest, as another experiment, we've removed elevation from all levels to see how much it actually affects the fun-factor of the game.

The playtest remains open, so make sure to request access and keep an eye on your email / steam library where it will pop up soon after!

Primary Changes:
- New Quest: Defend
- New Quest: Escort
- New Quest: Chicken Run
- Revamped Quest: Attack
- Revamped Quest: Ambush
- Added a new enemy spawner in the form of Porc Tents
- Replaced railroad overworld movement with free movement
- Added audio settings
- Added more & tweaked existing action VFX
- Removed elevation from all levels
- Added an 'action cam' system to make sure action targets are always in-frame

Happy Dobbeling!
